title: Best Flyer Designers (2026): How to Hire One That Works
description: How to hire a flyer designer: what the package should include, how to brief it, print and digital files, price factors and red flags.
intro: A flyer has seconds to tell someone what is happening, why it matters and what to do next. It may be printed, posted online, or both. Flyers fail when they try to say too much, when the print file does not match the printer's requirements, or when stock images are used without a license. This guide helps you order a flyer that is clear and ready to use.

faq.q: Do I need a print file and a digital version?
faq.a: Often both. A print file needs high resolution, bleed and the right color settings. A digital version for social media or email needs different sizes. Ask for both in one order if you will use both.
Bleed is extra image area beyond the edge of the page, which is trimmed off after printing. Without it, thin white lines can appear at the edges. Your printer will tell you how much they need.

faq.q: How much text should a flyer have?
faq.a: As little as possible: a headline, a few key details and one clear action. People glance at flyers; they rarely read them in full.

faq.q: Can the designer use stock photos?
faq.a: Yes, if they are licensed for commercial use. Ask where images come from, or send your own photos.

faq.q: Will I get an editable file?
faq.a: Ask for one if you plan to reuse the flyer for future events. A template lets you change dates and details without a new order.
